sections.content: nekem is the dative form of én ('I'), meaning roughly 'for me / to me'. Combined with jó ('good'), nekem jó says something suits or works for the speaker -- a common way to react to a suggested time.

items.spanish: Nekem nem jó délután, de este ráérek.
items.english: The afternoon doesn't work for me, but I'm free in the evening.
The evening works for me too.

sections.content: nekem jó doesn't use van -- it's the same zero-copula pattern as any predicate adjective sentence, just with nekem added to show who it's good for. Negate it with nem before jó: 'nekem nem jó'.
